pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: timerfd: Protect the might cancel mechanism proper BACKPORT NOTE: Minor conflict in timerfd_setup_cancel. The handling of the might_cancel queueing is not properly protected, so parallel operations on the file descriptor can race with each other and lead to list corruptions or use after free. Protect the context for these operations with a seperate lock. The wait queue lock cannot be reused for this because that would create a lock inversion scenario vs. the cancel lock. Replacing might_cancel with an atomic (atomic_t or atomic bit) does not help either because it still can race vs. the actual list operation. u2fd: Add U2FHID emulation daemon Emulate a U2FHID interface as defined by the FIDO Alliance 'FIDO U2F HID Protocol Specification' and forward the raw U2F APDU it has extracted (as defined by 'FIDO U2F Raw Message Formats'). The cr50 firmware in the TPM has an extension to process the U2F APDUs sent through a vendor defined command. The HID interface is used by the usual un-modified security key clients (e.g. the Chrome browser through the permission_broker). The daemon creates a new HID device from userspace using the UHID kernel interface and on the other side, it encapsulates the raw APDU into TPM vendor commands and feeds them to the cr50 firmware through the /dev/tpm0. BUG=b:35545754 TEST=pass U2FTest and HIDTest. HACK: hw_random: tpm-rng: don't access tpm when suspended hwrng_fillfn thread in core hwrng driver may still be generating initial randomness when the device is suspended. In this case tpm_rng_read() may send a GetRandom message to the tpm after the tpm state was saved in preparation to suspend, and thus cause the subsequent resume to fail. To prevent that, create a platform device for tpm-rng after the tpm is available in the system, handle suspend-resume callbacks and block tpm accesses while the device is suspended. A better method is implementing the tpm-rng 'plugin' for hwrng driver as a part of the tpm driver itself - calling hwrng_register() and handling suspend-resume there. Thus this patch is considered temporary and marked as HACK. BUG=b:63709621 TEST=Go through suspend-resume, check that tpm-rng is suspended before tpm0 and resumed after. Change-Id: I17e576482c84bc039d0e350b04b07577c4645bd5 Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/611403 Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

update_engine: Use the bsdiff library instead of its executable Currently we use bsdiff binary to generate BSDIFF and SOURCE_BSDIFF operations. This involves writing both the source and destination extents into disk and letting bsdiff read them again into memory. Now that we actually can use the bsdiff library itself, why not use the provided bsdiff library functions that can directly read source and destination data from the memory that we already have. This CL will reduce the patch generating time and memory footprint.
